text: Commercial money movement is a scale franchise: $18T processed in 2025 (wire, ACH, SWIFT, instant), self-reported #4 in real-time payments among banks, #8 ACH originator (ODFI) in Nacha's 2025 Top 50, sixth-largest commercial payments provider by revenue. Commercial payments revenue was $218M in 1Q26, +42% YoY including two months of Comerica (organic growth not disclosed) [S068,S069,S103,S951].

Newline by Fifth Third is the most transparently documented money-movement surface in the study set: public developer docs cover ACH (SEC codes, Same Day windows, returns/NOC/reversal/recall), RTP send/receive with queueing and VRNs, domestic wires, book transfers, webhooks; MCP server for AI agents (Dec 2025) [S044,S047,S048,S049,S088,S103].

Consumer inbound-money experience is strong: in-app payroll-login Direct Deposit Switch, Early Pay (2 days / refunds 5 days) with push notification, Extra Time cure window, Immediate Funds choice inside the mobile-deposit flow, Cardless ATM [S014,S061,S006,S002].
Zelle is cleanly integrated (Move Money > Send Money with Zelle), including business enrollment inside the consumer app, QR 'My Code', Zelle tags [S001,S003].

Comerica integration executed in ~7 months (merged 2/1/2026; conversion executed over Labor Day weekend, completed and announced 9/8/2026: ~600K accounts, 293 banking centers) with explicit payments transition playbooks (wires, ACH, FTD, EDM, international) [S100,S020,S024,S025].

Mobile app rated 4.8 (668K) / 4.7 (226K); J.D. Power #1 regional-bank mobile app satisfaction (2025); AI natural-language interface routes 'transfer funds' to task screens (6/2026) [S015,S016,S095,S097].

Commercial security controls are now fully documented: token-based two-factor for every wire/ACH origination and approval, Dual Administration Control, Dual Transaction Approval with unlimited Approval Workflows, customer-set daily limits that block approvals, PIN-wire call-backs above $250K, and bank transaction monitoring that halts suspect payments [S915].
Consumer Zelle flow includes a bank-documented in-flow name-mismatch warning and 'Suggested/Available' contact labelling that reduce misdirected payments [S902].
Fifth Third Direct mobile app (re-launched 2026) supports approve/decline/manage payments, RDC with continuous multi-check capture and role-based entitlements [S916,S917].
No self-service consumer/SMB wire transfer in the app or online banking — wires require a branch visit (peers offer digital wires) [S010,S011].
External (bank-to-bank) transfer product is effectively undocumented publicly: no marketing page, help article blocked to crawlers, verification/limits/cancel rules unknown [S106,S055,S017].
FedNow is not live for receive on converted accounts ('until further notice') and 'coming soon' on Newline, despite marketing a dual-network RTP+FedNow approach [S025,S043,S071].
No Paze participation; no documented push-to-card instant transfer; no consumer remittance product; Zelle is the only consumer instant rail [S082,S062].

Consumer-facing Zelle scam policy is thin: no public consumer reimbursement statement, no published in-flow interstitial content, one Zelle contact method per customer, limits disclosed only by phone or on the recipient screen [S001,S011,S013].
Support hours are published inconsistently (two different sets on the same Customer Service page); debit-card lock not offered (credit only) [S010,S007].

FedNow: Fifth Third Bank, N.A. is absent from the Federal Reserve's FedNow participant list as of 2026-11-02 (neither send nor receive), the FTD page says FedNow receipt is unavailable 'until further notice', and Newline still lists FedNow as 'coming soon' with no date [S924,S927,S925].

Migrated Comerica commercial clients lost RTP origination at conversion and are told to use same-day ACH or wires; Fifth Third Direct offers RTP receive only for them ($1 per received payment), so portal-based RTP send is not a standard FTD capability [S927].

Consumer wires are expensive and opaque: branch-only, $30/$50/$85 outgoing, no digital status or cancel right (except a 30-minute window on international Remittance Transfers), and the statement is the only notice [S930,S931].
Consumer bill pay publishes neither its cut-off time (shown only inside the interface) nor an expedited option; delivery method (check vs ACH) is chosen by the bank [S932].

Mobile app release notes are entirely generic ('Bug fixes and performance improvements') for every monthly release Jun 2025–Oct 2026, so customers get no in-store changelog of money-movement features [S918,S935].

Personal Banking FAQ wording on business accounts is ambiguous (reads as a send restriction; context suggests it concerns which Fifth Third accounts can receive) [S902][S975]; wire 'fees not published' on FAQs but listed in the welcome-kit PDF [S901][S907][S931].
Immediate Funds availability choice embedded in the mobile deposit step flow, priced per transaction [S006,S017].
Early Pay extended to business checking (merchant settlement/government deposits up to 2 days early) and to Comerica customers [S101,S099].
Instant Payments with Request for Payment early adoption and Account Validation API across ACH/wire/RTP [S018,S045].
Newline MCP Server + Skills for agentic payment integrations [S103].
Direct Express federal benefits financial agent (3.4M cardholders) with planned bill pay, cardless ATM and wallet features [S102].
Preferred Checking tier waives wire, stop-payment, cashier's check and money-order fees ('Complimentary wire transfers') rather than adding digital wire channels [S931].
Express Banking mobile deposits always use Immediate Funds (fee-based same-day availability) — an unusual mandatory-instant design for the entry-level account [S931].

Direct Express: Fifth Third is the U.S. Treasury's financial agent for the federal-benefits prepaid card (5-year agreement from 9/9/2025, ~3.4M cardholders). New enrollments with Fifth Third began May 2026, and Comerica-issued accounts migrate late 2026 / early 2027. Planned bill pay, cardless ATM and wallet features are bank-stated only [S102,S952].

The business Zelle page carries the network-standard sentence that qualifying imposter scams may be eligible for reimbursement; treated as a neutral statement (network minimum), not a strength, for parity with the other banks.

2025-12: Newline MCP Server; 2026-04-13 Skills added; 2025-12-09 Brex partnership [S103,S095].

2026-03-20: 'Plan' cash-flow and spending insights launched in the app's bottom navigation. Direct Deposit Switch (1,000+ employers) and Debit Card Tracker were existing features, both cited by May 2025 [S104,S920].
2026-06-02: SmartShield 'Report Phishing' in Fraud Center; 5M users [S098].

2026-06-17: AI-powered natural-language interface in mobile app routing to transfer/task screens [S097].

2026-10-19: Newline + Visa corporate cards in 40+ countries [S095].

2025-10: New 'Security Procedures for Commercial Wire Transfer, ACH Services, and Instant Payments' adds the API Access Channel (token auth, IP allow-listing) as a Security Procedure for Instant Payments [S915].

2026-07-01: Consumer fraud article restated the fraud-vs-scam reimbursement stance ('may not be able to get your money back' for authorized scam payments) and named the 'Pay Yourself' Zelle scam [S903].
2026-08-12: Jeanie named Best Chatbot (Tearsheet); 2.4M monthly app users, 150+ intents incl. 'transfer funds'/'sending money', 42% containment [S919].

2026-09-08: Comerica conversion — migrated commercial clients retain RTP receive only; FedNow receive unavailable; Fifth Third Direct mobile app re-listed on App Store (id6759976853, v2.2.0 by Nov 2026) [S927,S916].
2026-11-02: Fed FedNow participant list (1,973 FIs) still has no Fifth Third or Comerica entry [S924].
2026-05: New Direct Express enrollments begin with Fifth Third as financial agent; existing cardholder accounts to transition late 2026 / early 2027 [S952].

2025-04-11 (context, acquired entity): the CFPB dismissed without prejudice its Dec 2024 suit against Comerica Bank over Direct Express dispute and fraud-complaint handling (allegations only; never adjudicated). Comerica joined Fifth Third on 2026-02-01 and Fifth Third now serves as Direct Express financial agent [S979].
External transfer flow: verification method (micro-deposit vs instant), limits, timing, cancel rules, and whether an instant (push-to-card) option exists — help page blocked (robots) [S106].
Zelle: recurring/scheduled send, split, request cancellation, in-flow scam interstitial wording, consumer reimbursement stance.
Bill Pay: electronic vs check delivery, expedited payment, cutoff time values.
External transfer flow (verification, limits, timing, cancel) remains unpublished: linkpath.53.com help host now redirects to the homepage; requires a logged-in session [S932].

Zelle recurring/scheduled send, split and request cancellation: confirmed NOT published on any public page or FAQ; SmartShield 'Zelle fraud identification before you pay' interstitial copy still undocumented [S901,S902,S907,S908].
Bill pay: cut-off time value and any expedited/overnight option remain unpublished (DSUA: cut-off 'provided within the Bill Payment interface') [S932].
Consumer wire limits and cut-off times (Deposit Account Rules say cut-offs 'vary'; no values) [S930].

Push-to-card (Visa Direct / Mastercard Send): none found on public pages, the app listing or the Newline docs, so the chapter keeps false (INFERRED). A logged-in view of the external-transfer flow, or a bank or network statement, is needed to confirm absence (FITB-C014, UNRESOLVED).
Has Fifth Third, as the new Direct Express financial agent, changed the dispute and call-center handling the CFPB alleged against Comerica (suit dismissed without prejudice Apr 2025)? [S979]

Fifth Third Direct RTP origination: no portal screen evidenced (July 2026 initiation guide lists Account Transfers, Wire and ACH only [S973]; Security Procedures reference Instant Payments via Data Exchange/API [S915]); migrated Comerica clients told to use same-day ACH/wires [S927] — does any FTD client have portal RTP send?
